mnlCmntry.text: It's full time here at Atlanta Stadium and another late show by Argentina sees them beat England 2-1 and reach Sunday's World Cup final! After a low-key and cagey first half, the second burst into life in the 55th minute when Gordon smashed the Three Lions ahead after being picked out by Rogers' pinpoint delivery. Argentina turned the screw after falling behind, and Mac Allister saw a thumping header crash off the inside of the post. But Argentina got themselves level in the 85th minute when Fernandez, who had just seen a shot tipped over the crossbar, bent in a brilliant finish from distance. However, there was to be more late drama. Messi was once again the architect, this time crossing for Fernandez to head home and complete another dramatic World Cup turnaround for Scaloni's side at this year's finals. Argentina will feel they are deserved victors, given they registered an expected goals (xG) total of 1.84 from their 15 attempts to England's tally of 0.53 from just five shots. Argentina will advance for the chance to defend their title at New York New Jersey Stadium on Sunday, with Spain awaiting in what will pit Messi against Yamal for the first time. England, meanwhile, will face France in Saturday's third-place play-off. That is all from this live coverage. Catch you next time!
FULL TIME: ENGLAND 1-2 ARGENTINA

England once again try and pump a long ball into the box but Emiliano Martinez does brillianlty to come and collect when challenged by O'Reilly and Burn. The referee gives a foul against the goalkeeper and that is surely England's World Cup over.

Another needless flashpoint between the two sides erupts as Bellingham brings down Messi deep in his own half. Argentina now looking to slow the game right down and hold on for the win, while England look to try and muster up a miracle.

Pickford's long ball over the top misses every single England forward and Emiliano Martinez collects and falls to the floor and will take his time with getting the play restarted. England need a hero, but will anyone step forward?
Rashford is also thrown on in the England attack for the impressive Spence, who should not be on the losing side today. He has been immense.
mnlCmntry.title: Substitution

mnlCmntry.text: A final throw of the dice from Tuchel as he looks to save England. Toney comes on for his first appearance at this World Cup and replaces Stones.
mnlCmntry.title: Substitution

mnlCmntry.text: De Paul goes into the book after a heated discussion with Bellingham as England look to restart the action.
mnlCmntry.title: Yellow Card

mnlCmntry.text: Messi, once again, has inspired an Argentina comeback! Another pinpoint cross into the area is met by Lautaro Martinez, and the Inter striker does the rest! Messi has now either scored or assisted in each of his last 13 games for club and country combined, netting 14 goals and assisting 11.

GGGOOOAAALLL! LAUTARO MARTINEZ SURELY HEADS IN THE WINNING GOAL! Moments after Mac Allister had hit the post with a drive from just outside the box, Argentina take the lead through super sub Martinez! Messi collects the loose ball and chips a delicious cross onto the head of Martinez who heads beyond Pickford and breaks England hearts! Argentina find a way. That is what champions do! England 1-2 Argentina!
mnlCmntry.title: Goal - Header

mnlCmntry.text: The fourth official has indicated there will be a minimum of NINE additional minutes at the end of the second half. Can someone from either team make themselves a hero late on here?

Tuchel's decision to try and see the game out by bringing on defensive reinforcements could come back to bite him, with England now inviting the pressure on from Argentina for the final minutes of normal time. Stones is now down with an injury, but looks okay to continue after treatment.

And of course, it is Messi with yet another assist. There were replays to see if he was offside, but the Argentina captain was in the correct position and helps his team find another late goal at this World Cup! He has now scored or assisted in 11 consecutive World Cup appearances, extending the longest-ever run by a player on record since 1966.

GGGOOOAAALLL! ENGLAND'S RESISTANCE IS BROKEN BY FERNANDEZ! Moments after forcing a save from Pickford, Fernandez finds the back of the net with a stunning curling effort from 25 yards out into the bottom-left corner! We are level in this World Cup semi-final! England 1-1 Argentina!
mnlCmntry.title: Goal

mnlCmntry.text: ANOTHER SAVE FROM PICKFORD! Fernandez again tries his luck from distance, but Pickford does not take the risk and tips the ball over the crossbar. Corner for Argentina.

Messi looks to send another dangerous ball into the box, but the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner overhits his delivery and Pickford allows it to go out for a goal kick. A real pressure reliever for England, that!

Rice is also off having struggled with injuries and illness in the lead up to their clash against Norway, but Tuchel will want to keep him fresh should England make it to the final. O'Reilly is on in his place and is in midfield.
mnlCmntry.title: Substitution

mnlCmntry.text: James goes down and looks okay to carry on, but Tuchel is taking no chances. The towering presence of Burn is added into England's defence to try and defend the barrage of Argentina balls that will come into the box.
mnlCmntry.title: Substitution

mnlCmntry.text: Scaloni makes another change, and it really is all guns blazing here for the defending champions. Lautaro Martinez, who scored in Argentina's extra-time win against Switzerland, is on for Tagliafico.
mnlCmntry.title: Substitution

mnlCmntry.text: We're into the final 10 minutes here and at this moment in time, England are heading to Sunday's World Cup final! But, can they hold on?

GONZALEZ HEADS JUST WIDE! England are hanging on! Messi is again given time and space to clip the ball over the top and he finds Gonzalez, but his header narrowly evades the right post. The offside flag was up, but the replay showed he may have been onside!

OFF THE POST FROM MAC ALLISTER! De Paul, with his first involvement of the match, sends a sensational ball into the box and it finds the head of Mac Allister, but even with Pickford left stranded, his header cannons against the left post!
Both sets of players are now back out on the pitch and the action is back underway!

Tuchel also decides to make his first change of the match, and it looks to be a change in shape. Goalscorer Gordon is off for Konsa, who goes into the centre of defence, with Spence and James now in the wing-back positions.
mnlCmntry.title: Substitution

mnlCmntry.text: Molina also makes way, having been at fault for England's opener after losing Gordon. Montiel, the scorer of Argentina's winning penalty in the 2022 World Cup final, is on in his place.
mnlCmntry.title: Substitution

mnlCmntry.text: Another change in the Argentina defence sees Otamendi come on to replace Lisandro Martinez, who is on a yellow card.
mnlCmntry.title: Substitution

mnlCmntry.text: Another change for Scaloni during the hydration break, with Simeone, who has had a difficult outing, replaced by De Paul. This looks like a triple change for Argentina.
mnlCmntry.title: Substitution

mnlCmntry.text: We have another pause in play for the second hydration break of this World Cup semi-final. This second half has been electric from the start, with Gordon's goal the difference at Atlanta Stadium! Argentina have, however, grown into the game since going behind and a fine stop from Pickford denied Gonzalez from levelling things up. Scaloni's players are quickly back out on to the pitch, but England are taking their time.

WHAT A REACTION SAVE FROM PICKFORD! Messi is allowed time and space to deliver a dangerous ball into the box and it lands on the head of substitute Gonzalez, but the England number one is down low to thwart his attempt and England are able to clear the ball to safety!
Argentina are beginning to turn up the heat, here. Tagliafico attempts to whip a ball into the box, but Anderson is on hand to deflect the ball behind. Messi's corner is, however, cleared by Gordon.

RICE TRIES HIS LUCK! Kane sprays the ball out to James on the right-hand side as he ghosts in behind Tagliafico. He plays the ball back to Rice who winds up a strike, but it's comfortable for Emiliano Martinez to collect!

Scaloni is the first to turn to his bench. The experienced Paredes is withdrawn and on comes Atletico Madrid's Gonzalez. It looks like a shift in shape, with Fernandez dropping to the base of midfield.
mnlCmntry.title: Substitution

mnlCmntry.text: Now Argentina must try and break down this resolute England defence. This is not the first time the defending champions have faced adversity at this World Cup, but the manner of the game will certainly suit Tuchel's side, who will be hoping for a familiar defensive display to the one they had against Mexico in the last 16.

Gordon has been directly involved in six goals in his last seven games for England (two goals, four assists), after having just two goal involvements in his first 18 games for his country (two goals). He is also only the fourth Three Lions player to score at this year's World Cup, after Kane, Bellingham and Rashford!

WHAT A TACKLE FROM SPENCE! Fernandez is picked out in a pocket of space and sends Simeone on his way down the right, but just when the Atletico Madrid forward looks destined to score, across comes Spence to deliver a perfectly timed last-ditch challenge! The England left-back has had a sensational game so far!
In what is his first World Cup start, Rogers gets the assist, and a quite brilliant one at that! It was a bold move by Tuchel, but it has certainly paid off! That is why he's the England manager!

GGGOOOAAALLL! GORDON GIVES ENGLAND THE LEAD IN THIS SEMI-FINAL!!! Kane drops deep and tries to pick out Rogers, only for Lisandro Martinez to acrobatically clear the ball. Rice collects the loose ball and finds Rogers, who sends a sensational cross into the area for Gordon to steal in behind Molina and place past Emiliano Martinez! What a goal and what a start to this second half by England! England 1-0 Argentina!
mnlCmntry.title: Goal

mnlCmntry.text: Argentina come forward and Molina finds space on the right and delivers a dangerous ball into the area which is hacked clear by Bellingham. Paredes then curls a hopeful cross into the area trying to find Tagliafico, but it rolls behind for an England goal kick.

Romero goes into the book and joins his centre-back partner Lisandro Martinez on a yellow card. The ball breaks kindly for Bellingham, who looks to drive forward, but the Tottenham defender drags the England midfielder back with an arm around the middle and he's cautioned.
mnlCmntry.title: Yellow Card

mnlCmntry.text: It's a real end-to-end start to this second half, this time it's England's turn to come forward. Spence goes past Molina and crosses into a dangerous area but Argentina are able to clear their lines. More of the same, please!

ARGENTINA TWICE GO CLOSE! Emiliano Martinez is forced to go long, and Simeone does brilliantly to knock the ball down to Alvarez. He breaks free from Spence's challenge and forces Pickford into a smart stop at his near post. It breaks kindly again to the Argentine number nine, but his effort is deflected behind for a corner!
This is it then. Potentially, 45 minutes separates one of these two sides for a spot in Sunday's World Cup final. We're back underway at Atlanta Stadium, with Rice getting us up and running.

Given the nature of how things have played out in the opening 45 minutes, it is no surprise that the Opta supercomputer can see this ending in a draw and heading to extra time. It has predicted this semi-final to finish as a draw in normal time in 44.7% of its simulations. England are favoured to get the job done in 90 minutes with a 29.5% win probability to Argentina's 25.8%. The nerves on show are backed up by the match statistics, too. There were 19 fouls committed and 0 shots on target in the opening half between England and Argentina - the most fouls without an attempt on target in any half of football at this year's World Cup.

It's half-time here at Atlanta Stadium and it remains 0-0 between England and Argentina in this cagey yet feisty World Cup semi-final. Both teams have struggled to create any clear-cut chances thus far, with Stones' 33rd-minute header from Rice's free-kick the closest either side has come to breaking the deadlock. In fact, the combined expected goals (xG) between England and Argentina in the first half was just 0.08 - the lowest in the first half of a World Cup knockout stage match on record (since 1966). This semi-final is there for the taking, but will it be Argentina or England's abundance of attacking talent that will take the game by the scruff of the neck after the break?
HALF-TIME: ENGLAND 0-0 ARGENTINA
The fourth official has signalled there will be a minimum of three additional minutes at the end of the first half. Can either side find a winner before going in for the break?

And just after Anderson was given a yellow card, Lisandro Martinez is the first Argentina player to have his name taken. Rogers does well to wriggle his way around the Argentine number six, who holds him back and is rightly cautioned. One each for bookings.
mnlCmntry.title: Yellow Card

mnlCmntry.text: FERNANDEZ INCHES AWAY! Messi again opts to play the free-kick short and receives it back from Paredes, but his shot is blocked by Kane. The ball breaks kindly for Fernandez, who tries his luck from distance, and it arrows narrowly wide of the top-right corner!

As expected, Anderson is the first player into the book for his poorly timed challenge on Messi. No complaints from the Manchester City midfielder, now Argentina have a dangerous set-piece of their own.
mnlCmntry.title: Yellow Card

mnlCmntry.text: Here we go! Tensions are boiling over again! Messi skips beyond the challenge of Spence and Kane and looks to drive at the England defence but he is upended by Anderson. The challenge sees almost every Argentine player surround the referee and plenty of handbags are on show. The referee has done quite well to keep this one flowing, but that was certainly a foul.

England are growing into this now! Spence does brilliantly to press Simeone into making a mistake deep in his own half. Gordon plays a neat pass into Bellingham who draws a needless foul from Molina. Instead of Rice, James stands over this free-kick.

STONES GOES CLOSE! Rice, as he does so often for Arsenal, whips a delicious set-piece into the back post and finds Stones. The England defender rises high above Lisandro Martinez, but his attempt does not trouble Emiliano Martinez and ripples the side-netting.

Brilliant from Bellingham! After collecting the ball from deep, he sits Simeone down and drives at the Argentina defence, but as he approaches the box, he is chopped down by Fernandez. Rice and James stand over the resulting free-kick, which is in a very dangerous position.
Romero has been trying to make things work for Argentina. He has made six line-breaking passes, with this at least twice as many as any other player in the match so far (Anderson, three).

After taking on tactics and words of encouragement from their managers, England and Argentina come back out onto the pitch. The Three Lions do, however, need to find a way to get Kane into the game. He has had the fewest touches of any player in the match so far (four), while no Argentina player has had fewer than nine. Pickford gets us back underway!

The referee calls a halt to play for the game's first hydration break. After a fizzing start that saw Argentina attempt to ruffle England's feathers, both teams have struggled to find their rhythm, particularly in the final third. Tuchel and Scaloni are both down talking to their players, and you feel as though the first goal in this game will be crucial.

Simeone forces the first corner of the match after Messi takes a quick free-kick. The Atletico Madrid man drives to the right byline by Spence, who has had a fine start himself, blocks the ball behind.

Only three games at the 2026 World Cup have taken 20+ minutes before the game's first shot - two of them have been in England's last two games (29 v Norway, ongoing v Argentina), along with France against Paraguay (22). The Three Lions have threatened, more so than Argentina, but they will be hoping to try and really test Emiliano Martinez soon.

England work it well to the right-hand side as Kane, with his first real touches of this semi-final, picking out Rogers. The Aston Villa midfielder lays the ball on to the overlapping James who delivers first time into the box, but Emiliano Martinez is there to cut out the danger.
While there is not a lot between the sides in the opening stages, England do look slightly more comfortable in this semi-final as they look to take the game to Argentina early on here.

Messi again goes down under an England challenge, but his protests are waved away by the referee. Gordon comes away with possession and draws a foul from Simeone. It's an end-to-end start to this one, but neither side have been able to fashion a goal-scoring opportunity.

Argentina's four fouls are the joint-most by a side in the opening 10 minutes of a 2026 World Cup match, along with Sweden against France (four), and you feel as though that will be their gameplan throughout the encounter to try and disrupt England.

Anderson is again at the centre of attention here. He is tackled by Fernandez and the pair, while on the floor, tangle before Rogers is penalised with a coming together with Paredes. Referee Elfath calms things down and gives Argentina the free-kick, but Tuchel is far from impressed on the touchline.

Anderson has been everywhere in this opening 10 minutes. After Mac Allister's loose pass, he picks up possession and clips a ball down the left-hand side for Gordon to chase. He does reach the pass, but his cross is gathered by Emiliano Martinez.

The game still hasn't settled into any kind of rhythm as of yet. Rogers' first involvement sees him win a corner, but Rice's delivery fails to find an England shirt. James is then penalised for just being a little bit too tight when tussling with Tagliafico.

This time it's Argentina's turn to press. England do well and play themselves out of trouble from the back, but Anderson misplaces his pass, and that has woken up the travelling Argentina contingent inside the Atlanta Stadium. You just get the feeling this could go down as one of the great World Cup matches!

It's already heating up. Messi thinks he's owed a free-kick when Anderson wins possession back off him. But as the Manchester City midfielder lays the ball off, Fernandez comes right into the back of the England number eight with another late challenge. What a feisty opening to this World Cup semi-final!

England immediately win a throw in after putting Argentina under pressure early on. They control possession and win the first free-kick of the day with Paredes leaving a late one on Bellingham, just to let him know he's there in the first two minutes.
Referee Ismail Elfath blows his whistle and Messi gets this World Cup semi-final underway!

Here we go then. The national anthems have been sung. The final team talks have been done. It is now up to the players on the pitch to try and deliver on the World Cup stage. Kick off at Atlanta Stadium is just moments away!

Scaloni, meanwhile, has opted to make just one change to the team that battled their way past Switzerland last time out. Simeone, the son of Atletico Madrid boss and former Argentina international Diego, is selected to start and comes in to replace De Paul. With an average age of 29 years and 262 days, Argentina have named the fourth-oldest ever World Cup semi-final starting XI by any side, and oldest since France in 2006 v Portugal (30y 4d). All three sides to name an older semi-final XI won their tie (also Sweden 1958, Brazil 1962), and Scaloni will be hoping his experienced team can get the job done and set up a meeting with European champions Spain in the final. Messi will lead out the team and coming into this game, he has been directly involved in 46 goals in 54 semi-finals across his career (26 goals, 20 assists), including 11 in eight semi-final appearances for Argentina (four goals, seven assists).

Tuchel has opted to make three changes to the side that beat Norway last time out, with a significant alteration coming in attack. There are switches in both full-back positions as James, who picked up a hamstring injury against Ghana in the group stage, is preferred to Konsa. Spence is also handed a start ahead of Manchester City's O'Reilly. The big call comes on the right of the Three Lions' attack, with Rogers given his first World Cup start in place of Madueke. Kane, of course, captains the side and earns his 121st cap for England, the outright most of any outfield player for the Three Lions. Only Peter Shilton (125) has represented England more times, and the Bayern Munich striker will be hoping his milestone outing is a memorable one here.

ARGENTINA SUBS: Juan Musso, Marcos Senesi, Gonzalo Montiel, Rodrigo De Paul, Valentin Barco, Giovani Lo Celso, Geronimo Rulli, Exequiel Palacios, Nico Gonzalez, Thiago Almada, Nico Paz, Nicolas Otamendi, Jose Manuel Lopez, Lautaro Martinez, Facundo Medina.

ARGENTINA (4-4-2): Emiliano Martinez; Nicolas Tagliafico, Lisandro Martinez, Cristian Romero, Nahuel Molina; Enzo Fernandez, Alexis Mac Allister, Leandro Paredes, Giuliano Simeone; Julian Alvarez, Lionel Messi.

ENGLAND SUBS: Ezri Konsa, Nico O'Reilly, Bukayo Saka, Marcus Rashford, Trevoh Chalobah, Dean Henderson, Jordan Henderson, Dan Burn, Kobbie Mainoo, Ollie Watkins, Noni Maudeke, Eberechi Eze, Ivan Toney, James Trafford.
ENGLAND (4-2-3-1): Jordan Pickford; Djed Spence, Marc Guehi, John Stones, Reece James; Elliot Anderson, Declan Rice; Anthony Gordon, Jude Bellingham, Morgan Rogers; Harry Kane.

But if you thought England's journey to the semi-finals was full of thrills and spills, I present to you Argentina, who have had their fair share of close shaves on their way to this stage of the competition. They were taken to extra time by tournament debutants Cape Verde, before coming from two goals down to beat Egypt. They also needed additional-time goals from Julian Alvarez and Lautaro Martinez to battle past 10-man Switzerland in the quarter-finals, but there is no denying the fighting spirit within their ranks. Argentina have won all six of their matches at the 2026 World Cup, now their longest outright winning run in competition history. This will also be Argentina's sixth World Cup match against England, only ever playing Germany more times in the competition (also six vs the Netherlands), and all eyes will be on Lionel Messi. After his assist against Switzerland, Messi became the second player on Opta record (since 1966) to record 10+ goal contributions in multiple World Cups (2022 and 2026) after Kylian Mbappe (2022 and 2026), and you would expect him to have at least some say here. But enough chit-chat. With kick-off fast approaching, let's have a look to see who Tuchel and Scaloni have selected to start this eagerly anticipated World Cup semi-final, with their reward a tie with Luis de la Fuente's Spain at New York New Jersey Stadium in Sunday's showpiece!

England's World Cup campaign so far has been full of drama, and it was a familiar story in their quarter-final clash against Norway last time out. Jude Bellingham was the man of the hour once again for the Three Lions last time out, with his 93rd-minute winner completing his brace and a 2-1 comeback win to send Stale Solbakken's side rowing back home. England are contesting their fourth semi-final at a major tournament since 2018, as many as they had reached in their history prior to the World Cup in Russia (four). Tuchel's team have won their last four World Cup matches, their longest run since winning five in a row during their triumphant campaign in 1996 (five), though the England boss described their performance against Norway as "sloppy". However, England do have a favourable record against Argentina. They have lost just two of their 14 internationals against them (W6 D6), though their most recent defeat did come at the World Cup, going down 2-1 at the 1986 edition of the competition through Diego Maradona's brace, which will of course be remembered for the iconic "Hand of God" goal.
Hello and welcome to this LIVE commentary of the World Cup semi-final between Thomas Tuchel's England and defending champions Argentina at Atlanta Stadium!
